description: A complete action movie night: four classic public films and four original Signature features — every treatment with full synopsis, key scenes, cast, and viewing guide, curated to publish as-is.

items.title: Die Hard
items.logline: The definitive action film: one cop, one tower, one unforgettable Christmas.
items.synopsis: New York cop John McClane flies to Los Angeles to reconcile with his estranged wife Holly at her company's Christmas party in the Nakatomi Plaza tower. When German thief Hans Gruber and his crew seize the building and take the partygoers hostage, McClane — shoeless, outgunned, and alone — wages a one-man guerrilla war through the tower's vents, shafts, and stairwells. Gruber's crew systematically cracks the vault while McClane picks them off, aided by radio contact with skeptical LAPD officer Al Powell. As the FBI's heavy-handed tactics escalate the danger, McClane must stop Gruber from escaping with $640 million in bearer bonds and save Holly, culminating in a rooftop and window-ledge showdown.

scenes.title: The vault breach
scenes.text: Gruber's crew drills the seven locks while McClane watches from the vents.

scenes.title: The 'Yippee-ki-yay' moment
scenes.text: McClane drops a terrorist's body onto the police car with a taunting message.

scenes.title: The glass-shard walk
scenes.text: barefoot McClane pulls glass from his feet in the bathroom — the film's most human moment.

scenes.title: The rooftop explosion
scenes.text: the FBI's helicopter assault ends in fire as McClane escapes down a fire hose.

scenes.title: The final fall
scenes.text: Gruber plummets from the 30th floor, still clutching Holly's watch.

items.viewing_guide: Watch for how the film grounds spectacle in vulnerability — McClane bleeds, limps, and doubts. Note the clockwork plotting: every setup (the watch, the gold, Powell's backstory) pays off. Best viewed loud, with attention to Rickman's controlled menace.
items.description: The definitive action film: one cop, one tower, one unforgettable Christmas.

items.title: Mad Max: Fury Road
items.logline: A two-hour chase that never stalls: the action film as pure cinema.
items.synopsis: In a post-apocalyptic wasteland, drifter Max Rockatansky is captured by the warlord Immortan Joe's War Boys. When Joe's lieutenant Imperator Furiosa betrays him — fleeing with his five prized wives in a war rig — Max is strapped to the front of a pursuit vehicle as a blood donor. After a spectacular road battle, Max joins Furiosa's escape toward the legendary Green Place. Pursued by Joe's armada across the desert, the mismatched crew discovers the Green Place is a poisoned swamp, and chooses to turn back and take the Citadel itself. The film becomes a relentless high-speed war for the rig, ending with Joe's death and the wives' triumphant return to free the water-starved citadel.

scenes.title: The opening chase
scenes.text: Max strapped to the war rig, the Doof Warrior's flaming guitar wailing.

scenes.title: The sandstorm
scenes.text: the convoy drives into a towering fire-and-lightning storm.

scenes.title: The pole-cats
scenes.text: War Boys on swinging poles attack the rig mid-drive.

scenes.title: The night swamp
scenes.text: the rig bogs down; Furiosa learns the Green Place is gone.

scenes.title: The final run
scenes.text: the rig threads the canyon as Joe's rig crashes — the Citadel gates open.

items.viewing_guide: Watch as a masterclass in visual storytelling — the plot is told almost entirely through action. Notice the center-framed editing that keeps the chaos legible. The feminist core (Furiosa's arc) gives the mayhem meaning; track how Max moves from cargo to ally.

items.title: The Matrix
items.logline: The film that made philosophy an action genre.
items.synopsis: Hacker Neo learns from the mysterious Morpheus that his reality is a simulation — the Matrix — built by machines that harvest human bodies for energy. Offered the red pill, Neo wakes in the real world and joins Morpheus's crew aboard the hovercraft Nebuchadnezzar. As Morpheus believes Neo is 'the One' prophesied to free humanity, the crew is betrayed by Cypher to the relentless Agent Smith. Neo must master the Matrix's rules — there is no spoon — rescue Morpheus, and confront Smith in a reality-bending duel that ends with Neo seeing the Matrix's code and defeating the Agents, promising humanity's liberation.

scenes.title: The red pill
scenes.text: Morpheus's offer in the construct — the film's philosophical hinge.

scenes.title: The lobby shootout
scenes.text: Neo and Trinity rescue Morpheus in a ballet of bullet-time.

scenes.title: The helicopter rescue
scenes.text: 'Dodge this' — Trinity's impossible shot.

scenes.title: The subway fight
scenes.text: Neo vs. Agent Smith, learning to believe.

scenes.title: The awakening
scenes.text: Neo rises, sees the code, and destroys Smith from within.

items.viewing_guide: Watch for the layered influences — cyberpunk, anime, philosophy, Hong Kong action — fused into something new. The 'bullet time' technique changed action cinema; notice how the film earns its ideas with clear rules. The sequels expand the mythology; this one is the cleanest statement.

items.title: John Wick
items.logline: Grief as an action engine: the most stylish revenge film of its era.
items.synopsis: Legendary hitman John Wick has retired for love, but after his wife's death, her final gift — a puppy named Daisy — is killed by Iosef Tarasov, son of Russian mob boss Viggo. The killing unleashes Wick, the Baba Yaga the underworld fears. Viggo puts a bounty on his former enforcer, but Wick tears through the criminal world — the Red Circle club, the Continental Hotel's neutral ground, a church full of laundered money — with methodical, gun-fu precision. As Viggo's empire burns, Wick faces his old friend Marcus's sacrifice and finally confronts Viggo himself, ending the vendetta bloodied but unbowed, adopting a new dog as dawn breaks.

scenes.title: The home invasion
scenes.text: the inciting cruelty, played with restraint.

scenes.title: The Red Circle
scenes.text: Wick's nightclub assault — the 'gun-fu' showcase.

scenes.title: The Continental
scenes.text: the underworld's rules explained over drinks with Winston.

scenes.title: The church
scenes.text: Wick burns Viggo's fortune — the money, not just the men.

scenes.title: The final duel
scenes.text: Wick vs. Viggo in the rain, knives and exhaustion.

items.viewing_guide: Watch for the world-building — the Continental's coin economy, the clean, rule-bound underworld. The action choreography (long takes, judo-inflected gunplay) rewards attention to geography: you always know where Wick is. Note how little dialogue Wick needs.

items.title: The Last Map
items.description: Signature original action feature: Riley Fox inherits a golden idol and a one-way ticket to the Andes high passes.
items.logline: Riley Fox inherits a golden idol and a one-way ticket to the Andes high passes.
items.synopsis:
ACT 1 — The Call of the Wild
They made camp under strange stars. a golden idol pulsed on Riley Fox's chest. Somewhere out there, the smuggler queen was moving. The race, Riley Fox thought, was already on. action — time to prove it.

ACT 2 — Into the Green
At dawn the markers led to the ruins: stone teeth in the jungle's jaw. Riley Fox stood at the gate with a golden idol humming louder. 'Whatever happens,' Riley Fox said, 'we go together.'

ACT 3 — The Ruins
Riley Fox took it and ran, because Riley Fox is not an idiot. The chase through the collapsing ruins was the kind of thing they'd tell for years: swinging, sliding, the pilot Anya with the rope, a golden idol in the bag, the whole place coming down.

ACT 4 — The Price of Gold
The trek out was worse than the trek in: the warlord's men's backup team, the river rising, the pilot Anya feverish from a scratch that turned ugly. Riley Fox carried the pilot Anya and a golden idol in turns, and learned what shoulders are for.

ACT 5 — The Real Treasure
action — Riley Fox wrote it in the expedition log, under the date, under the coordinates of the Andes high passes. Then closed the book. Then opened the new map.

ACT 6 — Next Horizon
The plane — or boat, or truck, or camel — was already arranged. It always is, when a golden idol calls. That's the thing about legends: they don't end. They just wait for the next believer.

scenes.title: Into the Green
scenes.text: At dawn the markers led to the ruins: stone teeth in the jungle's jaw. Riley Fox stood at the gate with a golden idol humming louder. 'Whatever happens,' Riley Fox said, 'we go together.'

scenes.title: The Ruins
scenes.text: They emerged into daylight as the gate sealed forever behind the smuggler queen's screams — no, wait. Riley Fox went back. Because action, and because no one gets left, not even the bad guys. They dragged the smuggler queen out by the collar.

scenes.title: The Price of Gold
scenes.text: The backup team wasn't loyal — just paid. When Riley Fox offered them the truth about the warlord's men's promises (empty) versus a share of the legitimate expedition rights (real), they lowered their weapons. Money talks. Truth talks louder.

scenes.title: The Real Treasure
scenes.text: the collector Blackwood got fifteen years and a memoir deal. Riley Fox got the kid's wide eyes and the pilot Anya's friendship and a new map already arriving by courier. No return address. Of course.

items.viewing_guide: Watch The Last Map with the sound up. Act one sets the action; act two turns it; act three pays everything off. Best with friends and zero spoilers.

By dawn they were over the Amazon basin, the green unrolling below like a held breath. Casey Drake checked a golden idol one more time. It hummed faintly, the way true things do when they're near their home.

ACT 2 — Into the Green
At dawn the markers led to the ruins: stone teeth in the jungle's jaw. Casey Drake stood at the gate with a golden idol humming louder. 'Whatever happens,' Casey Drake said, 'we go together.'

ACT 3 — The Ruins
They emerged into daylight as the gate sealed forever behind the mercenary Voss's screams — no, wait. Casey Drake went back. Because action, and because no one gets left, not even the bad guys. They dragged the smuggler queen out by the collar.

ACT 4 — The Price of Gold
the smuggler queen, bound and furious, offered everything: money, power, a share. Casey Drake listened politely and said no politely, which infuriated the mercenary Voss more than any insult. Some people can't be bought. Some treasures can't be sold.

ACT 5 — The Real Treasure
the warlord's men got fifteen years and a memoir deal. Casey Drake got the kid's wide eyes and the pilot Anya's friendship and a new map already arriving by courier. No return address. Of course.

ACT 6 — Next Horizon
the pilot Anya was packed before Casey Drake finished reading the note. 'Where to?' the pilot Anya asked. Casey Drake pointed at the map's edge, past the Amazon basin, past everything known. 'There,' Casey Drake said.

items.title: Treasure of the lost city of Zal
items.description: Signature original action feature: The last expedition vanished in the lost city of Zal. Morgan Steele goes to find a golden idol — and them.
items.logline: The last expedition vanished in the lost city of Zal. Morgan Steele goes to find a golden idol — and them.
items.synopsis:
ACT 1 — The Call of the Wild
Morgan Steele was fixing an engine when a golden idol arrived — by courier, no return address, with a note: 'You know what this is. Come to the lost city of Zal. Hurry.' Morgan Steele knew. Everyone in their line knew the legend.

ACT 2 — Into the Green
They were followed now; the scholar Dr. Elena Vance spotted the glint of scopes at dusk. the smuggler queen wasn't just ahead — the rival expedition was around. Morgan Steele doubled the watch and slept with a golden idol under their head.

ACT 3 — The Ruins
They emerged into daylight as the gate sealed forever behind the rival expedition's screams — no, wait. Morgan Steele went back. Because action, and because no one gets left, not even the bad guys. They dragged the smuggler queen out by the collar.

ACT 4 — The Price of Gold
the smuggler queen, bound and furious, offered everything: money, power, a share. Morgan Steele listened politely and said no politely, which infuriated the smuggler queen more than any insult. Some people can't be bought. Some treasures can't be sold.

ACT 5 — The Real Treasure
They stood before a golden idol one last time. It had started all this: the legend, the race, the ruin, the rescue. Morgan Steele saluted it. Some doors, once opened, stay open forever.

ACT 6 — Next Horizon
Morgan Steele took one last look at the lost city of Zal, green and gold and dangerous. It had given them a golden idol, and taken nothing they weren't willing to give. Fair trade.

scenes.title: Into the Green
scenes.text: Three days into the lost city of Zal, the trail went cold — and then hot: fresh boot prints, the mercenary Voss's mark, heading the same way. 'They're a day ahead,' the scholar Dr. Elena Vance said, 'but they're heavy. We're fast.'

scenes.title: The Ruins
scenes.text: Inside: wonders. the scholar Dr. Elena Vance, the scholar at heart, wept at the murals. Morgan Steele kept watch, because wonders in such places usually have teeth. They did: the floor was a trap, the walls were a trap, the air was a trap.

scenes.title: The Price of Gold
scenes.text: the collector Blackwood was delivered to the authorities with the evidence. a golden idol was delivered to the museum, on loan, with Morgan Steele's name on the plaque and the scholar Dr. Elena Vance's name right beside it, where it belonged.

scenes.title: The Real Treasure
scenes.text: The museum opening was black tie. Morgan Steele wore boots. the scholar Dr. Elena Vance, recovered and insufferable, wore a grin. a golden idol sat behind glass, humming faintly, home at last among people who'd care for it.

program:
"""Working demo for this playlist record: renderer + play-order simulator.
Run:  python3 playlist_demo.py          (prints the full playlist document)
      python3 playlist_demo.py play    (simulates playing it in order)
"""
import json, sys, time

PL = {'title': 'Action — Complete Movie Night', 'theme': 'action', 'week': 'L1', 'items': [{'n': 1, 'title': 'Die Hard', 'detail': 'John McTiernan'}, {'n': 2, 'title': 'Mad Max: Fury Road', 'detail': 'George Miller'}, {'n': 3, 'title': 'The Matrix', 'detail': 'The Wachowskis'}, {'n': 4, 'title': 'John Wick', 'detail': 'Chad Stahelski'}, {'n': 5, 'title': 'The Last Map', 'detail': 'Signature Pictures'}, {'n': 6, 'title': 'Casey Drake and the a golden idol', 'detail': 'Signature Pictures'}, {'n': 7, 'title': 'Treasure of the lost city of Zal', 'detail': 'Signature Pictures'}, {'n': 8, 'title': 'The a jade compass Expedition', 'detail': 'Signature Pictures'}], 'curator_notes': 'Action night 1: open with a beloved classic, follow with a Signature original, and close with the strongest film of the eight. Four public classics anchor the night; four Signature features show what comes next. Every entry is the full treatment.'}

def render():
    print("=" * 64)
    print(PL["title"].upper())
    print(PL["theme"])
    print("=" * 64)
    for it in PL["items"]:
        print("%2d. %s — %s" % (it["n"], it["title"], it["detail"]))
    print("\n--- curator notes ---\n" + PL["curator_notes"])

def play():
    render()
    print("\n▶ now playing (simulated order):")
    for it in PL["items"]:
        print("  ♪ %s ..." % it["title"])
        time.sleep(0.15)
    print("■ end of playlist — %d items" % len(PL["items"]))

if __name__ == "__main__":
    (play if len(sys.argv) > 1 and sys.argv[1] == "play" else render)()

items.title: Raiders of the Lost Ark
items.logline: The adventure template every film since has chased.
items.synopsis: In 1936, archaeologist Indiana Jones races Nazi agents to find the lost Ark of the Covenant. After a booby-trapped South American temple costs him a golden idol to rival Belloq, Indy is recruited by U.S. intelligence: the Nazis are digging at Tanis, Egypt. Reuniting with fiery Marion Ravenwood — whose father's headpiece holds the key to the Ark's location — Indy follows the trail through Cairo's streets, a truck chase, and a hidden map room. Captured after the Ark is unearthed, Indy and Marion are tied to a post as Belloq opens the Ark in a Nazi ceremony — and the Ark's divine wrath destroys the Nazis while Indy survives by closing his eyes.

scenes.title: The boulder
scenes.text: the opening temple escape — cinema's greatest cold open.

scenes.title: The Cairo chase
scenes.text: Indy shoots the swordsman — improvisation that became legend.

scenes.title: The map room
scenes.text: sunlight through the headpiece reveals the Well of Souls.

scenes.title: The truck chase
scenes.text: Indy dragged under, then over, the Nazi convoy.

scenes.title: The Ark opened
scenes.text: faces melt — the supernatural payoff.

items.viewing_guide: Watch the serial-adventure structure: each set piece tops the last. Notice how Indy is competent but vulnerable — he loses constantly and survives by grit. The film respects archaeology just enough to make the fantasy land. Karen Allen's Marion is no damsel; track her agency.

items.title: Jurassic Park
items.logline: The blockbuster that made CGI real — and made us fear it.
items.synopsis: Billionaire John Hammond clones dinosaurs from DNA preserved in amber and builds a theme park on Isla Nublar. To win investor approval after a worker's death, he invites paleontologists Alan Grant and Ellie Sattler, chaos theorist Ian Malcolm, and his grandchildren for a preview tour. Saboteur Dennis Nedry disables the park's power to steal embryos, freeing the dinosaurs. Grant and the kids survive a T. rex attack; Malcolm is wounded; the raptors hunt the survivors through the park. In the control room, Ellie restores power while the raptors corner the group — until the T. rex returns, and the survivors escape by helicopter as Hammond's dream collapses.

scenes.title: The first brachiosaurus
scenes.text: the reveal — wonder before terror.

scenes.title: The T. rex paddock
scenes.text: the goat, the fence, the lawyer on the toilet.

scenes.title: The raptor kitchen
scenes.text: the kids outsmart the pack hunters.

scenes.title: The sick triceratops
scenes.text: the film's quiet, humane center.

scenes.title: The banner fall
scenes.text: 'When Dinosaurs Ruled the Earth' — the T. rex's roar.

items.viewing_guide: Watch the Spielberg craft: the dinosaurs are revealed slowly, mostly in daylight — a radical choice that the CGI earns. Notice the theme stated plainly ('life finds a way') and dramatized in every scene. The film is pro-science and anti-hubris at once.

items.title: The Mummy
items.logline: Swashbuckling horror-adventure: the most fun you'll have in Egypt.
items.synopsis: In 1920s Egypt, librarian Evelyn Carnahan and her brother Jonathan hire brash adventurer Rick O'Connell to find the lost city of Hamunaptra. A rival American expedition races them there. Evelyn reads from the Book of the Dead, accidentally resurrecting Imhotep, a mummified high priest cursed 3,000 years ago. Imhotep regenerates by consuming the Americans and pursues Evelyn — the reincarnation of his lost love. Rick, Evelyn, and Jonathan battle mummy priests, scarabs, and a Cairo possessed by plagues, finally defeating Imhotep by reading from the Book of Amun-Ra and escaping Hamunaptra with its treasure as the city collapses.

scenes.title: The Hamunaptra race
scenes.text: the two expeditions' comic charge across the desert.

scenes.title: The awakening
scenes.text: Evelyn reads the Book; Imhotep's eyes open.

scenes.title: The scarab
scenes.text: the flesh-eating beetle under the skin — the film's gross-out peak.

scenes.title: The Cairo plagues
scenes.text: locusts, hail, and darkness over the city.

scenes.title: The final reading
scenes.text: the Book of Amun-Ra strips Imhotep's immortality.

items.viewing_guide: Watch as a throwback to 1930s serials — romance, comedy, and horror in balance. Fraser and Weisz's chemistry carries the quieter scenes; notice how Evelyn's bookishness, not just Rick's guns, saves the day. The CGI shows its age; the charm doesn't.

items.title: Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl
items.logline: The pirate movie that launched a billion-dollar fleet.
items.synopsis: Blacksmith Will Turner and Governor's daughter Elizabeth Swann are drawn into the world of pirates when the cursed crew of the Black Pearl — undead skeletons by moonlight — kidnaps Elizabeth for her gold medallion. To save her, Will frees the eccentric Captain Jack Sparrow, who wants the Pearl back from mutineer Barbossa. The trio's uneasy alliance sails to the Isla de Muerta, where Barbossa needs Elizabeth's blood to lift the Aztec curse. In a moonlit cave battle, Jack and Barbossa duel while Will breaks the curse, and Jack's cunning saves the day — though he ends the film dangling at the gallows, rescued by Will's loyalty.

scenes.text: sinking boat, perfect step onto the dock.

import json, sys, time

PL = {'title': 'Adventure — Complete Movie Night', 'theme': 'adventure', 'week': 'L2', 'items': [{'n': 1, 'title': 'Raiders of the Lost Ark', 'detail': 'Steven Spielberg'}, {'n': 2, 'title': 'Jurassic Park', 'detail': 'Steven Spielberg'}, {'n': 3, 'title': 'The Mummy', 'detail': 'Stephen Sommers'}, {'n': 4, 'title': 'Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl', 'detail': 'Gore Verbinski'}, {'n': 5, 'title': "Treasure of Sahara's deep erg", 'detail': 'Signature Pictures'}, {'n': 6, 'title': 'Taylor Brooks and the a carved obelisk key', 'detail': 'Signature Pictures'}, {'n': 7, 'title': "Treasure of Sahara's deep erg", 'detail': 'Signature Pictures'}, {'n': 8, 'title': 'Beyond the machete', 'detail': 'Signature Pictures'}], 'curator_notes': 'Adventure night 2: open with a beloved classic, follow with a Signature original, and close with the strongest film of the eight. Four public classics anchor the night; four Signature features show what comes next. Every entry is the full treatment.'}

def render():
    print("=" * 64)
    print(PL["title"].upper())
    print(PL["theme"])
    print("=" * 64)
    for it in PL["items"]:
        print("%2d. %s — %s" % (it["n"], it["title"], it["detail"]))
    print("\n--- curator notes ---\n" + PL["curator_notes"])

def play():

    print("\n▶ now playing (simulated order):")
    for it in PL["items"]:
        print("  ♪ %s ..." % it["title"])
        time.sleep(0.15)
    print("■ end of playlist — %d items" % len(PL["items"]))

if __name__ == "__main__":

items.title: Toy Story
items.logline: The film that proved animation could carry adult emotion.
items.synopsis: Woody, a pull-string cowboy doll, is the beloved leader of Andy's toys — until Andy's birthday brings Buzz Lightyear, a space-ranger action figure who believes he's real. Consumed by jealousy, Woody's attempt to sideline Buzz backfires, stranding both at a Pizza Planet. Captured by the toy-torturing neighbor Sid, the rivals must escape his mutilated-toy lair. Buzz's crisis — discovering he's mass-produced — is healed by Woody's wisdom: being loved by a child is what matters. They rocket back to Andy's car on Sid's rocket, arriving just as the family moves, cementing their friendship.

items.title: Spirited Away
items.logline: Animation's first Oscar winner — a masterpiece about growing up.
items.synopsis: Ten-year-old Chihiro wanders with her parents into an abandoned theme park that becomes a bathhouse for spirits at nightfall. Her parents are transformed into pigs; Chihiro is trapped and must work for the witch Yubaba, who steals her name (renaming her Sen). Befriended by the mysterious Haku, Chihiro labors in the bathhouse, befriends the lonely No-Face, and journeys to the witch's twin sister Zeniba to return a stolen seal. Through courage and kindness, Chihiro frees Haku from Yubaba's control, reclaims her name, and breaks her parents' curse — leaving the spirit world with her memory of it fading.

items.title: The Lion King
items.logline: Disney's crown jewel: Shakespeare on the savanna.
items.synopsis: Lion cub Simba, heir to the Pride Lands, is tricked by his uncle Scar into believing he caused his father Mufasa's death in a wildebeest stampede. Scar seizes the throne; Simba flees and is raised by the carefree meerkat Timon and warthog Pumbaa on a 'Hakuna Matata' philosophy. Years later, the lioness Nala finds him and reveals Scar's tyranny has ruined the kingdom. Guided by the shaman Rafiki and Mufasa's spirit, Simba returns, confronts Scar — exposing the murder — and reclaims his place in the Circle of Life as the rains return.

items.title: Shrek
items.logline: The fairy tale that ate the fairy tale.
items.synopsis: The ogre Shrek, who cherishes his swamp's solitude, finds it invaded by fairy-tale exiles dumped there by the diminutive Lord Farquaad. To win his swamp back, Shrek agrees to rescue Princess Fiona from a dragon-guarded tower — accompanied by the relentlessly talkative Donkey. On the journey, Shrek and the secretly ogre-by-night Fiona fall in love, while Farquaad plans to marry her for legitimacy. At the wedding, Shrek crashes the ceremony; Fiona's curse breaks at true love's kiss — transforming her permanently into an ogress, and the two marry in the swamp as the fairy-tale world celebrates.

items.title: Groundhog Day
items.logline: The comedy that became a philosophy textbook.
items.synopsis: Cynical TV weatherman Phil Connors is sent to Punxsutawney for the Groundhog Day festival and wakes the next morning to find the same day repeating endlessly. After confusion comes hedonism — robbery, gluttony, seduction — then despair and repeated suicide attempts, all resetting at 6 a.m. Gradually Phil uses the loop to genuinely improve: learning piano, ice sculpting, saving lives around town, and truly knowing producer Rita. When he finally spends a perfect day selflessly loving the town and Rita, the loop breaks — he wakes on February 3rd, a changed man.

items.title: Mrs. Doubtfire
items.logline: Williams at his most heartfelt — comedy with a father's soul.
items.synopsis: Voice actor Daniel Hillard's chaotic parenting costs him custody after his divorce from Miranda. Desperate to see his kids, Daniel — a master of voices — disguises himself as the elderly British nanny 'Mrs. Doubtfire' and is hired by his ex-wife. As Doubtfire, Daniel becomes the stable presence his children need, while juggling his real identity, a new job, Miranda's suave suitor Stu, and a court liaison's scrutiny. The ruse collapses at a restaurant where Daniel must be both himself and Doubtfire at once. Though the lie costs him custody, the judge grants visitation — and Daniel, as Doubtfire's TV host, teaches that families take many forms.

items.title: A Puzzle in the riverside inn
items.description: Signature original comedy feature: Mildred Quill and librarian Miss Faye must untangle a web of secrets centered on a pressed flower.
items.logline: Mildred Quill and librarian Miss Faye must untangle a web of secrets centered on a pressed flower.
items.synopsis:
ACT 1 — Tea and Tidings
librarian Miss Faye arrived before the tea was poured, full of the news: the masked visitor had been seen about the riverside inn at dawn, asking questions nobody liked. 'Mildred Quill,' said librarian Miss Faye, 'there's a mystery brewing, and you're the only one with the nose for it.'

ACT 2 — The Missing Piece
librarian Miss Faye brought the parish records, and together they found the gap: a name missing where a name should be, a date that did not fit. a pressed flower was the key, Mildred Quill was certain; it unlocked a story someone had paid to keep shut.

ACT 3 — Questions at Dusk
But Mildred Quill shook her head. Something was missing — a motive with a human heart in it. a pressed flower was not mere property; it was a promise, or a debt, or a love. She would find which before she accused anyone.

ACT 4 — The Storm Breaks
the charming stranger appeared then, wild-eyed, and confessed before Mildred Quill could speak: it had begun as a kindness, grown into a theft, and ended in a lie that poisoned the riverside inn. 'I never meant —' began the disgraced solicitor, and could not finish.

ACT 5 — The Reckoning
the rival shopkeeper's motive, when all heard it, drew more pity than anger — a lost inheritance, a sick child, a desperate choice. the riverside inn was stern, but the riverside inn was also kind; and kindness found a way to help where the law could only punish.

ACT 6 — Quiet After
librarian Miss Faye brought flowers — 'for the best detective in the county,' they said, gruff as ever. Mildred Quill put them in water and told them not to be silly, but she kept the card.

scenes.title: The Missing Piece
scenes.text: At the riverside inn, the landlord remembered the jealous heir drinking alone, turning a pressed flower over and over. 'Nervous hands,' he said. 'Guilty hands, if you ask me.' Mildred Quill asked him, and wrote it down.

scenes.title: Questions at Dusk
scenes.text: librarian Miss Faye kept watch from the garden gate while Mildred Quill asked about a pressed flower. the silent partner claimed never to have seen it — but described it perfectly, down to the scratch on its side. Mildred Quill noted that, too.

scenes.title: The Storm Breaks
scenes.text: They walked back through the storm with the evidence wrapped in oilcloth. librarian Miss Faye said nothing, but their silence was agreement. comedy — even on the worst night, Mildred Quill thought, especially then.

scenes.title: The Reckoning
scenes.text: The constable did his duty, but Mildred Quill had already done hers: she had made the truth plain, so that no whisper could twist it. librarian Miss Faye squeezed her hand. 'Neatest case I ever saw,' they whispered.

items.logline: When the disgraced solicitor is seen near the market town of Bramblewick, Mildred Quill follows the trail of a brass key.
items.synopsis:
ACT 1 — Tea and Tidings
That evening Mildred Quill spread her notes on the parlor table: a map of the market town of Bramblewick, a list of names, and a brass key in the center like a spider. 'Someone,' she said to the cat, 'is lying. And I mean to find out who.'

ACT 2 — The Missing Piece
That night she dreamed of the market town of Bramblewick with all its windows lit, and every window hiding something. She woke knowing the next step: confront the one person who had not been questioned — the rival shopkeeper himself.

ACT 3 — Questions at Dusk
At dusk she walked to the old vicarage alone, turning a brass key in her pocket. The answer, she felt, was close — as close as the church bell that began to toll, counting out the hours like clues.

ACT 4 — The Storm Breaks
the masked visitor appeared then, wild-eyed, and confessed before Mildred Quill could speak: it had begun as a kindness, grown into a theft, and ended in a lie that poisoned the market town of Bramblewick. 'I never meant —' began the masked visitor, and could not finish.

ACT 5 — The Reckoning
On market day Mildred Quill laid it all before the market town of Bramblewick: a brass key, the letters, the photograph, the confession. The crowd in the square was silent as a church. the jealous heir stood with head bowed and did not deny a word.

ACT 6 — Quiet After
the rival shopkeeper, from wherever the law had sent him, wrote a letter of thanks: for the truth, for the pity, for the chance to begin again. Mildred Quill read it twice and filed it with the case notes.

items.title: The Godfather
items.logline: The crime epic against which all others are measured.
items.synopsis: In 1945, Don Vito Corleone — the aging head of a New York crime family — refuses to enter the narcotics trade, provoking a war with rival families. After an assassination attempt leaves the Don wounded, his reluctant youngest son Michael — a war hero who wanted out — takes charge: ordering hits, outmaneuvering rivals, and descending into the violence he once rejected. As Vito dies and Michael consolidates power — baptizing his nephew while his enemies are murdered — he becomes the new Don, colder than his father, and his wife Kay realizes the man she married is gone.

scenes.title: The door closes

items.viewing_guide: Watch Brando's mumbling, cat-stroking Don — a performance built from stillness. Notice Coppola's operatic structure: family ritual (weddings, baptisms, funerals) as the frame for murder. The film romanticizes nothing; track Michael's face hardening scene by scene.

items.title: Goodfellas
items.logline: The mob movie as adrenaline rush — and cautionary tale.
items.synopsis: Henry Hill grows up idolizing the Lucchese crime family and works his way from errand boy to associate, alongside Jimmy Conway and the psychotic Tommy DeVito. The film traces three decades: the 1960s rise (the Lufthansa heist), the good life of money and power, and the cocaine-fueled 1980s paranoia that destroys it all. After Tommy's murder and Jimmy's betrayal, Henry — strung out and hunted — turns FBI informant, entering witness protection as a 'schnook' in suburbia, lamenting the end of the gangster life.

items.viewing_guide: Watch Scorsese's kinetic style — freeze frames, needle drops, fourth-wall narration — as the subject: the filmmaking is as coked-up as Henry. Notice the domestic horror: Karen's complicity, the family's rot. The last shot (Tommy firing at the camera) breaks the spell deliberately.

The stories interlock through the diner robbery that opens and closes the film, with Jules's Ezekiel 25:17 speech reframing violence as a path to redemption.

items.title: The Shawshank Redemption
items.logline: The most beloved film ever made about hope.
items.synopsis: Banker Andy Dufresne is wrongly convicted of murdering his wife and sentenced to life at Shawshank prison. Befriended by the lifer Red, Andy endures brutality with quiet dignity — building a library, helping inmates earn degrees, and secretly tunneling through his cell wall behind a poster. After the warden murders the one witness who could prove Andy's innocence, Andy escapes through the sewers during a thunderstorm, having embezzled the warden's laundered money. He exposes the corruption; the warden kills himself; Red is paroled and follows Andy's clues to a Mexican beach, where the friends reunite.

items.synopsis:
ACT 1 — The Client
'I need you to find out what this means,' the client said, laying a key to a locker on the desk like a bet. Hank Mercer had seen a hundred such objects. They all meant the same thing: somebody was lying, and somebody was going to bleed.

ACT 2 — The Streets Talk
Back at the office, Hank Mercer spread the pieces out: a key to a locker, the ledger page, Ruby's note. The shape of it was the fixer, big as a building. And Hank Mercer was just one detective with a gun and a grudge against lies.

ACT 3 — The Dame's Story
Hank Mercer took photographs with hands that didn't shake. Evidence. The one thing the fixer couldn't buy, beat, or bury. a key to a locker had led here, as a key to a locker always does, to the rotten center.

ACT 4 — The Squeeze
Ruby's club was next — a fire in the kitchen, a message in the smoke. Hank Mercer found her unharmed and furious, and that fury was worth ten guns. 'End this,' she said. Hank Mercer intended to.

ACT 5 — The Confrontation
It went down the way it always goes: shouting, threats, a gun that Hank Mercer was faster than. When the police took the dame with the red scarf out, the old waterfront seemed to exhale, like a drunk finally telling the truth.

ACT 6 — Last Call
The dame left town on the morning train, brother in tow, free and clean. She left Hank Mercer a note: 'You were the only honest thing in it.' Hank Mercer kept the note. Detectives keep everything.

"""Working demo for this playlist record: renderer + play-order simulator.
Run:  python3 playlist_demo.py          (prints the full playlist document)
      python3 playlist_demo.py play    (simulates playing it in order)
"""
import json, sys, time

PL = {'title': 'Crime — Complete Movie Night', 'theme': 'crime', 'week': 'L5', 'items': [{'n': 1, 'title': 'The Godfather', 'detail': 'Francis Ford Coppola'}, {'n': 2, 'title': 'Goodfellas', 'detail': 'Martin Scorsese'}, {'n': 3, 'title': 'Pulp Fiction', 'detail': 'Quentin Tarantino'}, {'n': 4, 'title': 'The Shawshank Redemption', 'detail': 'Frank Darabont'}, {'n': 5, 'title': 'The Long Night', 'detail': 'Signature Pictures'}, {'n': 6, 'title': 'Rain on Grand Central Station', 'detail': 'Signature Pictures'}, {'n': 7, 'title': 'Shadows Over Grand Central Station', 'detail': 'Signature Pictures'}, {'n': 8, 'title': 'Dead End Street', 'detail': 'Signature Pictures'}], 'curator_notes': 'Crime night 5: open with a beloved classic, follow with a Signature original, and close with the strongest film of the eight. Four public classics anchor the night; four Signature features show what comes next. Every entry is the full treatment.'}

def render():
    print("=" * 64)
    print(PL["title"].upper())
    print(PL["theme"])
    print("=" * 64)
    for it in PL["items"]:
        print("%2d. %s — %s" % (it["n"], it["title"], it["detail"]))
    print("\n--- curator notes ---\n" + PL["curator_notes"])

def play():
    render()
    print("\n▶ now playing (simulated order):")
    for it in PL["items"]:
        print("  ♪ %s ..." % it["title"])
        time.sleep(0.15)
    print("■ end of playlist — %d items" % len(PL["items"]))

if __name__ == "__main__":
    (play if len(sys.argv) > 1 and sys.argv[1] == "play" else render)()

items.title: March of the Penguins
items.logline: Nature documentary as epic — endurance made beautiful.
items.synopsis: Narrated with novelistic warmth, the film follows emperor penguins through their annual breeding cycle in Antarctica. Each winter, the penguins march up to 70 miles inland to their breeding grounds, where females lay a single egg and return to the sea — leaving males to incubate the egg through months of blizzards, huddling for warmth. The mothers return to feed the chicks; both parents shuttle between sea and colony until the chicks fledge. The film documents the cycle's brutal attrition — storms, predators, starvation — and the species' extraordinary endurance.

items.viewing_guide: Watch the anthropomorphism debate the film sparked — the narration gives the penguins human-like motives, which critics questioned and audiences loved. items.title: Free Solo
items.logline: The documentary as ethical thriller — exhilarating and unsettling.
items.synopsis: The film follows climber Alex Honnold's quest to free-solo (climb without ropes) El Capitan's 3,000-foot Freerider route in Yosemite — a feat never attempted. The documentary captures two years of preparation: Honnold's meticulous rehearsal with ropes, his spartan emotional life, his relationship with girlfriend Sanni, and the filmmakers' ethical torment over filming a possible death. On June 3, 2017, Honnold climbs the route in under four hours. The camera crew, positioned to capture it, barely dares to watch — and the film becomes as much about the cost of witnessing as the climb itself.

items.title: Won't You Be My Neighbor?
items.logline: A documentary that makes grown adults weep — on purpose.
items.synopsis: The documentary traces Fred Rogers's life and the 33-year run of 'Mister Rogers' Neighborhood' — from his early puppetry and theological studies to the show's radical gentleness: addressing assassination, divorce, and death directly to children. Through archival footage and interviews with family, cast, and crew, the film reveals Rogers's private struggles — his weight, his temper, his doubts — and his public battles, including his famous 1969 Senate testimony that saved public broadcasting. It argues that Rogers's philosophy of radical kindness was a deliberate moral stance, not naiveté.

items.title: Planet Earth
items.logline: The nature documentary as global event.
items.synopsis: The BBC's landmark series surveys Earth's biomes across eleven episodes: pole to pole, mountains, fresh water, caves, deserts, ice worlds, great plains, jungles, shallow seas, seasonal forests, and ocean deep. Using revolutionary high-definition and time-lapse photography, it captures snow leopards hunting, birds of paradise dancing, great white sharks breaching, and wildebeest migrations — narrated by David Attenborough. The series documents both splendor and fragility, with each episode's 'diaries' revealing the extraordinary efforts behind the shots.

The ruins of the Siberian taiga were a puzzle built by people who didn't want visitors. a carved obelisk key was the key — literally; it fit a slot in the great door, and the stone sighed open after a thousand years.

ACT 4 — The Price of Gold
the warlord's men, bound and furious, offered everything: money, power, a share. Sam Wilder listened politely and said no politely, which infuriated the rival expedition more than any insult. Some people can't be bought. Some treasures can't be sold.

items.title: Pan's Labyrinth
items.logline: The darkest fairy tale — fantasy as resistance.
items.synopsis: In 1944 Francoist Spain, young Ofelia moves with her pregnant mother to the mill commanded by her brutal stepfather, Captain Vidal. Escaping into a labyrinth, Ofelia meets the Faun, who says she's the reincarnated Princess Moanna and must complete three tasks to reclaim her throne. As Vidal's cruelty escalates — torturing rebels, murdering innocents — Ofelia's tasks grow darker: the toad, the Pale Man's feast (where she eats the forbidden grapes), and the final choice: the Faun demands her baby brother's blood, and Ofelia refuses. Vidal shoots her; she dies — and the film's final ambiguity blooms: Ofelia enthroned in the underworld, or a dying child's fantasy.

items.synopsis:
ACT 1 — The Call
Dorian Ash slept that night with the rune glowing faintly, and dreamed of Dragonpeak in flames. They woke with the taste of smoke and a single thought: fantasy.

ACT 2 — Trials of the Road
The road through Dragonpeak tested them daily: a bridge held by a troll who demanded riddles, a forest where the trees walked, a river that flowed uphill. the elf Luthien Silverleaf's wit and Dorian Ash's courage saw them through each.

ACT 3 — The Descent
To reach the Crown of Thorns, they had to descend into the Witch Queen Morwen's domain: a fortress of black glass where the sun never shone. the elf Luthien Silverleaf picked the locks; Dorian Ash carried the light — a single coal of hope in the dark.

ACT 4 — The Price
the elf Luthien Silverleaf woke and wept to see it. 'The prophecy—' they began. Dorian Ash said: 'Prophecies are poems, not orders.' But the army of the usurper Lord Vane was coming, and they had no magic left.

ACT 5 — The Breaking of the Dark
the Crown of Thorns, dark and cold so long, blazed sudden white — fed not by magic but by the choice. The light struck the dragon Karthax's armor and the armor was empty; the dark lord was only a frightened soul inside, and the soul, seen, fled.

ACT 6 — The Return
They came home to Dragonpeak in spring, when the orchards bloomed. The songs had already arrived ahead of them, as songs do, and every verse was wrong in the details and right in the heart.

ACT 1 — The Call
Finnian Vale was mending a fence in the Whispering Woods when the sky went dark at noon. The elders whispered: the necromancer Sylas had taken the Last Dragon Egg, and the old magic was failing. Prophecy or not, someone had to go.

ACT 2 — Trials of the Road

the Last Dragon Egg blazed at Finnian Vale's touch, recognizing its bearer. Power flooded through them — and with it, the terrible knowledge of its price. Every magic, the seer had said, is a promise. This one demanded everything.

ACT 4 — The Price
They escaped the fortress by griffon, the Last Dragon Egg burning like a small sun. But the ranger Tam Oaken was wounded, and the wound festered with dark magic. The healers said only the Last Dragon Egg itself could cure it — at the cost of its power.

ACT 5 — The Breaking of the Dark
The battle for the Whispering Woods raged from dawn to dusk. the dragon Karthax rode out in black armor, terrible and splendid, and challenged Finnian Vale single combat. The armies held their breath.

ACT 6 — The Return
the Last Dragon Egg was set in the great hall, where children touch it for luck. It never blazed again — but on dark nights, travelers swear it glows faintly, like a coal that remembers fire.

the Crown of Thorns, dark and cold so long, blazed sudden white — fed not by magic but by the choice. The light struck the dragon Karthax's armor and the armor was empty; the dark lord was only a frightened soul inside, and the soul, seen, fled.

"""Working demo for this playlist record: renderer + play-order simulator.
Run:  python3 playlist_demo.py          (prints the full playlist document)
      python3 playlist_demo.py play    (simulates playing it in order)
"""
import json, sys, time

PL = {'title': 'Fantasy — Complete Movie Night', 'theme': 'fantasy', 'week': 'L8', 'items': [{'n': 1, 'title': 'The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring', 'detail': 'Peter Jackson'}, {'n': 2, 'title': "Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone", 'detail': 'Chris Columbus'}, {'n': 3, 'title': 'The Princess Bride', 'detail': 'Rob Reiner'}, {'n': 4, 'title': "Pan's Labyrinth", 'detail': 'Guillermo del Toro'}, {'n': 5, 'title': 'Light of Dragonpeak', 'detail': 'Signature Pictures'}, {'n': 6, 'title': 'Light of the Whispering Woods', 'detail': 'Signature Pictures'}, {'n': 7, 'title': 'The usurper Lord Vane War', 'detail': 'Signature Pictures'}, {'n': 8, 'title': 'The Shadow of the usurper Lord Vane', 'detail': 'Signature Pictures'}], 'curator_notes': 'Fantasy night 8: open with a beloved classic, follow with a Signature original, and close with the strongest film of the eight. Four public classics anchor the night; four Signature features show what comes next. Every entry is the full treatment.'}

def render():
    print("=" * 64)
    print(PL["title"].upper())
    print(PL["theme"])
    print("=" * 64)
    for it in PL["items"]:
        print("%2d. %s — %s" % (it["n"], it["title"], it["detail"]))
    print("\n--- curator notes ---\n" + PL["curator_notes"])

def play():
    render()
    print("\n▶ now playing (simulated order):")
    for it in PL["items"]:
        print("  ♪ %s ..." % it["title"])
        time.sleep(0.15)
    print("■ end of playlist — %d items" % len(PL["items"]))

if __name__ == "__main__":
    (play if len(sys.argv) > 1 and sys.argv[1] == "play" else render)()

items.title: Schindler's List
items.logline: The Holocaust film — a memorial in cinema.
items.synopsis: In Nazi-occupied Poland, businessman Oskar Schindler — a profiteer and Nazi Party member — staffs his factory with Jewish workers for cheap labor, managed by the accountant Itzhak Stern. As the Holocaust escalates — the Kraków ghetto liquidation, the horrors of Plaszów under the sadistic Amon Goeth — Schindler is transformed by what he witnesses. He spends his fortune bribing officials to keep his workers, compiling 'Schindler's List' of 1,100 Jews to transfer to a new factory. He saves them; broken by the war's end, he weeps that he could have saved more. The survivors place stones on his grave.

items.title: Braveheart
items.logline: The historical epic as national myth.
items.synopsis: In 13th-century Scotland, William Wallace — whose father and brother were killed by the English — lives quietly until English soldiers murder his wife Murron. Wallace leads a rebellion that grows from vengeance to a national uprising: the victory at Stirling, the disastrous defeat at Falkirk after betrayal by Scottish nobles, and guerrilla war against the tyrannical King Edward I. Captured through betrayal, Wallace is tortured in London but refuses to submit, crying 'Freedom!' at his execution — inspiring Robert the Bruce to lead Scotland's final fight.

items.title: Gladiator
items.logline: The epic that brought Rome back to the screen.
items.synopsis: Roman general Maximus — beloved by the dying Emperor Marcus Aurelius — is chosen as successor over the emperor's corrupt son Commodus, who murders his father and orders Maximus executed. Maximus escapes but finds his family crucified; enslaved, he becomes a gladiator whose arena victories make him a hero of Rome. Brought to the Colosseum, Maximus becomes the people's champion against Commodus's tyranny, secretly plotting with the emperor's sister Lucilla. In the final duel, the wounded Maximus kills Commodus and dies, reuniting with his family in the afterlife as Rome is freed.

items.title: Lincoln
items.logline: The political drama as American scripture.
items.synopsis: In January 1865, President Abraham Lincoln — the Civil War nearly won — fights to pass the Thirteenth Amendment abolishing slavery before the war's end removes the political leverage. The film focuses on the legislative battle: Lincoln's backroom deals, patronage promises, and moral arm-twisting of lame-duck Democrats, aided by the radical Thaddeus Stevens (who must hide his egalitarianism) and opposed by peace Democrats. The amendment passes by two votes; Lincoln is assassinated days after the war ends, and the film closes with his second inaugural's promise of 'malice toward none.'

historical — Beatrice Lovell had it carved, finally, on no monument at all, just lived it, in a country manor, in every ordinary, extraordinary day.

items.logline: The horror film as puzzle box — endlessly debated.

The hotel's violent past — a previous caretaker murdered his family — seeps into Jack through visions and the ghostly bartender Lloyd. Danny's 'shining' reveals the truth: the hotel wants him. Jack descends into madness, hunting his family with an axe through the hedge maze. Wendy and Danny escape in the snow; Jack freezes to death in the maze. The final photograph — Jack at a 1921 party — suggests the hotel has absorbed him forever.

a music box that plays itself, mended, sits on the mantel. It doesn't play, or fill, or show. It's just an object now — which is to say, it's just a story. Sarah Okafor keeps it to remember: horror.

ACT 6 — Epilogue: The Light Kept
Years later, Sarah Okafor still walks the abandoned mill at night, checking the rooms the way you check on sleeping children. The nursery is a study now. The cold spot is just a draft. Mostly.

"""
import json, sys, time

Four public classics anchor the night; four Signature features show what comes next. Every entry is the full treatment.'}

def render():
    print("=" * 64)
    print(PL["title"].upper())
    print(PL["theme"])

    for it in PL["items"]:

items.logline: The whodunit, reinvented — a donut with a hole.
items.synopsis: Famous novelist Harlan Thrombey is found dead after his 85th birthday party — apparent suicide, but the police hire the flamboyant detective Benoit Blanc. ACT 1 — Tea and Tidings
That evening Edith Plum spread her notes on the parlor table: a map of Thistledown Hall, a list of names, and a missing will in the center like a spider. 'Someone,' she said to the cat, 'is lying. And I mean to find out who.'

ACT 2 — The Missing Piece
A note came then, unsigned: 'Stop asking about a missing will.' Edith Plum read it twice, smiled, and pinned it to her board. Threats, she told Miss Violet Crowe, are confessions in a hurry.

ACT 3 — Questions at Dusk
Back in the parlor, Edith Plum laid out the evidence: the landlord's tale, the parish gap, the threatening note, the too-perfect description. Miss Violet Crowe whistled. 'It's a noose,' they said, 'and the masked visitor tied it.'

ACT 4 — The Storm Breaks
The storm that had threatened Thistledown Hall all week broke at last, rattling the windows of Thistledown Hall. In the midst of it came a hammering at Edith Plum's door: Miss Violet Crowe, soaked, with news — the silent partner had been seen digging near the old vicarage.

ACT 5 — The Reckoning
That evening the kettle sang again in her cottage, and Edith Plum wrote the last line in her journal: Truth told, justice done, neighbors mended. mystery — I shall drink tea to that.

ACT 6 — Quiet After
the disgraced solicitor, from wherever the law had sent him, wrote a letter of thanks: for the truth, for the pity, for the chance to begin again. Edith Plum read it twice and filed it with the case notes.

The morning Dorothy Lark found a torn letter on the doorstep of her cottage in Hollyhock Lane, the kettle had just begun to sing. She turned the object over in her hands, frowning, for it plainly belonged to someone — and someone in Hollyhock Lane was missing it badly.

Dorothy Lark found the silent partner at the edge of Hollyhock Lane, packing a bag in a great hurry. 'Leaving us?' she asked pleasantly, and the jealous heir's smile did not reach the eyes. Every answer was smooth, and every smooth answer was a lie.

ACT 4 — The Storm Breaks
Dorothy Lark listened to the end, rain running off her cape. Justice, she said quietly, was not the same as punishment; but the truth belonged to everyone in Hollyhock Lane, and it would be told.

the masked visitor's motive, when all heard it, drew more pity than anger — a lost inheritance, a sick child, a desperate choice. Hollyhock Lane was stern, but Hollyhock Lane was also kind; and kindness found a way to help where the law could only punish.

ACT 6 — Quiet After
And if another mystery comes to Hollyhock Lane — as mysteries do, like weather — Dorothy Lark will be ready, kettle on, journal open. For mystery, always, in Hollyhock Lane and everywhere.

items.logline: The noir you watch for the detective, not the mystery.
items.synopsis: Private eye Philip Marlowe is hired by the dying General Sternwood to handle a blackmailer targeting his wild younger daughter Carmen. items.synopsis: In 1912, the penniless artist Jack Dawson wins a third-class ticket on the Titanic and falls for Rose DeWitt Bukater, a first-class girl engaged to the cruel Cal Hockley. As the ship sinks, Jack and Rose fight for survival through the flooding corridors; Jack sacrifices his place on the floating debris, dying in the Atlantic. Elderly Rose, having lived a full life, returns to drop the Heart of the Ocean into the sea — and dreams of reunion on the grand staircase.

items.title: Pride & Prejudice
items.logline: Austen's romance — pride humbled, prejudice dissolved.
items.synopsis: In Regency England, the sharp-tongued Elizabeth Bennet spars with the proud Mr. Darcy, whose first proposal — insulting her family even as he declares love — she rejects. Through Darcy's letter (revealing Wickham's villainy), Elizabeth's visit to Pemberley, and Lydia's elopement (secretly saved by Darcy), her prejudice dissolves as his pride humbles. Darcy's second proposal — at dawn, in the mist — is the romantic corrective: 'You have bewitched me, body and soul.' The film ends with the Bennets' blessing and the couple's happiness.

items.logline: The greatest romance ever filmed — of love and sacrifice.
items.synopsis: In Vichy-controlled Casablanca, the cynical expatriate Rick Blaine — who 'sticks his neck out for nobody' — is confronted by his lost love Ilsa, now married to Resistance hero Victor Laszlo. In the film's immortal finale, Rick puts Ilsa on the plane with Laszlo — 'Here's looking at you, kid' — and shoots the Nazi Major Strasser, beginning 'a beautiful friendship' with Captain Renault. The personal is sacrificed to the political; the cynic becomes a patriot.

ACT 1 — Homecoming
The house was smaller than memory and larger than grief. In the attic, under a quilt, Grace Mitchell found a pressed wildflower — and with it, the whole of her seventeenth summer came back in a rush.

ACT 2 — The Thing Remembered
her best friend Jess listened to the whole story over coffee and said what best friends say: 'You have to talk to him.' Grace Mitchell said she couldn't. her best friend Jess said she must. They were both right.

ACT 3 — Complications
Her grandmother Rose's voice came back to her: 'The heart knows first, baby. The head just takes minutes.' Grace Mitchell stopped running. She turned around and went to find him.

ACT 4 — The Choice
her best friend Jess cried at the news and denied it. The whole of Maple Hollow seemed to conspire in their happiness: the bookshop stayed open late, the bakery made a cake, the wildflowers bloomed on schedule.

ACT 5 — The Promise
The wedding was in Maple Hollow, in the season of wildflowers. Her grandmother Rose's quilt was on the bed. her best friend Jess gave a speech that made everyone cry laughing.

ACT 6 — Epilogue in Wildflowers
romance. In Maple Hollow, in the wildflowers, in the salt air, in every sunset: the whole story, still beginning, never ending.

"""Working demo for this playlist record: renderer + play-order simulator.
Run:  python3 playlist_demo.py          (prints the full playlist document)
      python3 playlist_demo.py play    (simulates playing it in order)
"""
import json, sys, time

PL = {'title': 'Romance — Complete Movie Night', 'theme': 'romance', 'week': 'L14', 'items': [{'n': 1, 'title': 'Titanic', 'detail': 'James Cameron'}, {'n': 2, 'title': 'The Notebook', 'detail': 'Nick Cassavetes'}, {'n': 3, 'title': 'Pride & Prejudice', 'detail': 'Joe Wright'}, {'n': 4, 'title': 'Casablanca', 'detail': 'Michael Curtiz'}, {'n': 5, 'title': 'The a pressed wildflower Summer', 'detail': 'Signature Pictures'}, {'n': 6, 'title': 'Letters to Yesterday', 'detail': 'Signature Pictures'}, {'n': 7, 'title': 'The Long Way Home', 'detail': 'Signature Pictures'}, {'n': 8, 'title': 'Wildflower Hearts', 'detail': 'Signature Pictures'}], 'curator_notes': 'Romance night 14: open with a beloved classic, follow with a Signature original, and close with the strongest film of the eight. Four public classics anchor the night; four Signature features show what comes next. Every entry is the full treatment.'}

def render():
    print("=" * 64)
    print(PL["title"].upper())
    print(PL["theme"])
    print("=" * 64)
    for it in PL["items"]:
        print("%2d. %s — %s" % (it["n"], it["title"], it["detail"]))
    print("\n--- curator notes ---\n" + PL["curator_notes"])

def play():
    render()
    print("\n▶ now playing (simulated order):")
    for it in PL["items"]:
        print("  ♪ %s ..." % it["title"])
        time.sleep(0.15)
    print("■ end of playlist — %d items" % len(PL["items"]))

if __name__ == "__main__":
    (play if len(sys.argv) > 1 and sys.argv[1] == "play" else render)()

Obi-Wan falls to Darth Vader; Luke — trusting the Force over his targeting computer — destroys the station. items.logline: Captain Nix Halden inherits a distress beacon and a course for New Ceres Colony that the Void Syndicate will kill to stop.
items.synopsis:
ACT 1 — Launch
The klaxon woke Captain Nix Halden before the dawn cycle. On the viewscreen, New Ceres Colony glittered — and tumbling toward it, broadcasting on all bands, was a distress beacon. 'Dr. Ilsa Venn,' Captain Nix Halden said, 'plot an intercept. Quietly.'

ACT 2 — The Chart Unfolds
'It's a map,' breathed Captain Nix Halden, 'and a warning.' The route it drew cut through the worst of the drift: plasma storms, minefields, and the patrol lanes of Pirate Queen Vex.

ACT 3 — Storm Season
A mine took their port array. The deck went dark, then red. Dr. Ilsa Venn was already moving, cable in teeth, splicing by feel. 'Talk to me,' Captain Nix Halden said, and Dr. Ilsa Venn talked — numbers, jokes, anything to keep the fear small.

ACT 4 — The Traitor's Price
Then a distress beacon spoke — fully, at last. Not a map but a key, and not to a place but to a shield: an ancient defense grid sleeping around New Ceres Colony, the only thing that could stop Admiral Sarn's fleet.

ACT 5 — The Grid Awakens
The duel was legend before it ended: two ships in the fire-light, neither yielding, until Captain Nix Halden did the impossible — dove through the grid's own gate, which a distress beacon held open, and watched the Hollow Fleet break against the shield they could not see.

ACT 6 — Home Signal
And when the next distress call came — as it always does, out in the drift — the engines were already warm. There are always more skies. There is always New Ceres Colony, somewhere, needing its heroes.

scenes.text: Dr. Ilsa Venn cracked a distress beacon's casing with a spanner and a prayer. Inside: coordinates, a starlog, a voice saying one word over and over — the name of New Ceres Colony.

scenes.title: Storm Season
scenes.text: The battle was short and ugly. Captain Nix Halden used the storm itself as a weapon, luring the flagship into a plasma surge that stripped its shields. They escaped in the glare, hull scorched, crew cheering raggedly.

scenes.title: The Traitor's Price
scenes.text: Captain Nix Halden laughed for the first time in days. 'All this way,' they said, 'and we were carrying the lock, not the treasure.' Dr. Ilsa Venn was already calculating the wake-up sequence.

scenes.text: The flagship came on anyway, and Captain Nix Halden met it ship to ship above the burning sky. It was the Void Syndicate themselves on the viewscreen, offering one last deal. Captain Nix Halden answered with the engines at full burn.

items.synopsis:
ACT 1 — Launch
They grappled a quantum compass with the cargo arm as the first raider shells crossed their bow. the android Echo whooped as the airlock sealed. Whatever a quantum compass was, it was theirs now — and Admiral Sarn knew it.

ACT 2 — The Chart Unfolds
the android Echo cracked a quantum compass's casing with a spanner and a prayer. Inside: coordinates, a starlog, a voice saying one word over and over — the name of Station Meridian.

ACT 3 — Storm Season
Afterward, Captain Mara Voss looked at each face on the bridge and said it plainly: 'There's a traitor aboard. I don't know who. But a quantum compass goes to Station Meridian — with all of us, or with whoever's left.'

ACT 4 — The Traitor's Price
the android Echo caught them at the airlock. There was no fight — only the traitor crying that Admiral Sarn held their family. Captain Mara Voss understood, and hated understanding. Mercy, out here, was a luxury with teeth.

ACT 5 — The Grid Awakens
Silence, then. The grid humming. Station Meridian safe below. the android Echo put a hand on Captain Mara Voss's shoulder and said what everyone was thinking: 'We live.'

ACT 6 — Home Signal
They landed at Station Meridian to crowds and bells. The old voice from the starlog had belonged to the grid's last keeper, dead a hundred years; a quantum compass was their final message. Captain Mara Voss laid it in the memorial with honors.

ACT 1 — Launch
Engineer Pip Solano ran the numbers with grease on their hands and worry in their eyes. 'Pirate Queen Vex has three ships in the drift,' they said. 'If we burn hard, we can make it. If we burn hard, everyone will see us.'

ACT 2 — The Chart Unfolds
'It's a map,' breathed Commander Dax Renn, 'and a warning.' The route it drew cut through the worst of the drift: plasma storms, minefields, and the patrol lanes of the Void Syndicate.

ACT 3 — Storm Season
A mine took their port array. The deck went dark, then red. Engineer Pip Solano was already moving, cable in teeth, splicing by feel. 'Talk to me,' Commander Dax Renn said, and Engineer Pip Solano talked — numbers, jokes, anything to keep the fear small.

ACT 4 — The Traitor's Price
The traitor showed themselves at the third waypoint: the signal officer, paid in promises by Admiral Sarn. They seized a star chart etched in crystal and ran for the escape pod with Admiral Sarn's ships closing in.

ACT 5 — The Grid Awakens
Silence, then. The grid humming. New Ceres Colony safe below. Engineer Pip Solano put a hand on Commander Dax Renn's shoulder and said what everyone was thinking: 'We live.'

ACT 6 — Home Signal
And when the next distress call came — as it always does, out in the drift — the engines were already warm. There are always more skies. There is always New Ceres Colony, somewhere, needing its heroes.

scenes.title: The Chart Unfolds
scenes.text: The crew voted — that was Commander Dax Renn's rule, always a vote before a suicide run. Every hand went up. Engineer Pip Solano grinned. 'We didn't sign on for safe,' they said.

scenes.title: Storm Season
scenes.text: Afterward, Commander Dax Renn looked at each face on the bridge and said it plainly: 'There's a traitor aboard. I don't know who. But a star chart etched in crystal goes to New Ceres Colony — with all of us, or with whoever's left.'

scenes.title: The Traitor's Price
scenes.text: Then a star chart etched in crystal spoke — fully, at last. Not a map but a key, and not to a place but to a shield: an ancient defense grid sleeping around New Ceres Colony, the only thing that could stop Admiral Sarn's fleet.

scenes.title: The Grid Awakens
scenes.text: The flagship came on anyway, and Commander Dax Renn met it ship to ship above the burning sky. It was the Hollow Fleet themselves on the viewscreen, offering one last deal. Commander Dax Renn answered with the engines at full burn.

items.description: Signature original scifi feature: Commander Ash Korv inherits a coded starlog and a course for Port Andromeda that the Void Syndicate will kill to stop.
items.logline: Commander Ash Korv inherits a coded starlog and a course for Port Andromeda that the Void Syndicate will kill to stop.
items.synopsis:
ACT 1 — Launch
In the hold, under work lights, Commander Ash Korv studied a coded starlog. It pulsed faintly, like a heart. 'scifi,' Commander Ash Korv murmured. 'Let's find out what you are.'

ACT 2 — The Chart Unfolds
'It's a map,' breathed Commander Ash Korv, 'and a warning.' The route it drew cut through the worst of the drift: plasma storms, minefields, and the patrol lanes of Warlord Krell.

ACT 3 — Storm Season
The plasma storm hit at the second waypoint, a wall of fire across the sky. Dr. Ilsa Venn rerouted everything to the shields, hands flying, while Commander Ash Korv threaded the ship through gaps that opened and closed like eyes.

ACT 4 — The Traitor's Price
Then a coded starlog spoke — fully, at last. Not a map but a key, and not to a place but to a shield: an ancient defense grid sleeping around Port Andromeda, the only thing that could stop Pirate Queen Vex's fleet.

ACT 5 — The Grid Awakens
Silence, then. The grid humming. Port Andromeda safe below. Dr. Ilsa Venn put a hand on Commander Ash Korv's shoulder and said what everyone was thinking: 'We live.'

ACT 6 — Home Signal
The traitor's family was found and freed; the traitor wept and was forgiven, and signed on again — this time for real. Commander Ash Korv's rule about second chances held, barely, and gloriously.

scenes.title: The Chart Unfolds
scenes.text: The crew voted — that was Commander Ash Korv's rule, always a vote before a suicide run. Every hand went up. Dr. Ilsa Venn grinned. 'We didn't sign on for safe,' they said.

scenes.title: Storm Season
scenes.text: Through the fire they saw it: the Void Syndicate's flagship, waiting in the storm's eye like a spider. 'They knew the route,' Commander Ash Korv said. 'Someone sold the starlog.' The betrayal sat cold in their stomach.

scenes.title: The Traitor's Price
scenes.text: Commander Ash Korv let them live, confined to quarters. 'Admiral Sarn trades in hostages,' Commander Ash Korv told the crew. 'We trade in something better.' It was a gamble; the crew's eyes said they knew it.

scenes.title: The Grid Awakens
scenes.text: The duel was legend before it ended: two ships in the fire-light, neither yielding, until Commander Ash Korv did the impossible — dove through the grid's own gate, which a coded starlog held open, and watched Warlord Krell break against the shield they could not see.

items.title: Rocky
items.logline: The underdog film — heart over hardware.
items.synopsis: Philadelphia club fighter Rocky Balboa — a debt collector with a good heart — gets a once-in-a-lifetime shot at heavyweight champion Apollo Creed, who wants a novelty 'Italian Stallion' opponent. Rocky trains with the grizzled Mickey, romances the shy Adrian, and discovers his real goal isn't winning but going the distance — proving he's not 'just another bum.' The fifteen-round fight ends in a split decision for Creed, but Rocky has won what matters: Adrian's love, the crowd's roar, and his own dignity.

items.title: Remember the Titans
items.logline: The sports film as American parable.
items.synopsis: In 1971 Alexandria, Virginia, the newly integrated T.C. Williams High School hires Black coach Herman Boone over the white incumbent Bill Yoast. Forced to integrate his team, Boone's brutal camp forges unity — the players learn each other's souls, not just plays. Through the season, Boone and Yoast navigate racism from the school board (which wants Boone to fail), the town, and themselves. The team goes undefeated to the state championship, winning on a final trick play — and the film's epilogue reveals the lifelong bonds, and Gerry Bertier's paralysis and death, with grace.

items.title: Hoosiers
items.logline: The small-town sports film — perfection.
items.synopsis: In 1950s Indiana, the disgraced coach Norman Dale — hiding a past scandal — takes over the tiny Hickory High basketball team. With only seven players, Dale's fundamentals-first discipline clashes with the town's love of its star Jimmy Chitwood, who refuses to play. Dale wins the town over game by game, recruits the alcoholic Shooter as assistant, and earns Jimmy's return. The team storms the state tournament, culminating in the championship: the final play — 'I'll make it' — and Jimmy's shot at the buzzer. Hickory, the smallest school, becomes state champions.

items.title: The Karate Kid
items.logline: The mentor film — wisdom in work gloves.
items.synopsis: New Jersey transplant Daniel LaRusso is bullied in California by the Cobra Kai dojo's Johnny Lawrence. The handyman Mr. Miyagi — hiding his own grief — agrees to train Daniel, but the training is unorthodox: waxing cars, sanding floors, painting fences. The chores are muscle memory; Daniel learns karate without knowing it. At the All-Valley tournament, Daniel faces Johnny in the final — injured, he wins with the crane kick. Miyagi's mentorship — 'wax on, wax off' — becomes pop culture's shorthand for hidden wisdom.

items.description: Signature original sports feature: The last expedition vanished in the lost city of Zal. Sam Wilder goes to find a golden idol — and them.
items.logline: The last expedition vanished in the lost city of Zal. Sam Wilder goes to find a golden idol — and them.
items.synopsis:
ACT 1 — The Call of the Wild
The landing was rough — it always is — and the lost city of Zal swallowed them whole: heat, noise, green. the pilot Anya grinned. 'Just like old times.' Sam Wilder grinned back. Old times had nearly killed them twice.

ACT 2 — Into the Green
At dawn the markers led to the ruins: stone teeth in the jungle's jaw. Sam Wilder stood at the gate with a golden idol humming louder. 'Whatever happens,' Sam Wilder said, 'we go together.'

ACT 3 — The Ruins
The ruins of the lost city of Zal were a puzzle built by people who didn't want visitors. a golden idol was the key — literally; it fit a slot in the great door, and the stone sighed open after a thousand years.

ACT 4 — The Price of Gold
the rival expedition, bound and furious, offered everything: money, power, a share. Sam Wilder listened politely and said no politely, which infuriated the mercenary Voss more than any insult. Some people can't be bought. Some treasures can't be sold.

ACT 5 — The Real Treasure
sports — Sam Wilder wrote it in the expedition log, under the date, under the coordinates of the lost city of Zal. Then closed the book. Then opened the new map.

ACT 6 — Next Horizon
Engines up. sports. The horizon, as always, was just the beginning.

scenes.title: Into the Green
scenes.text: Three days into the lost city of Zal, the trail went cold — and then hot: fresh boot prints, the rival expedition's mark, heading the same way. 'They're a day ahead,' the pilot Anya said, 'but they're heavy. We're fast.'

scenes.title: The Ruins
scenes.text: the mercenary Voss's team hit them in the treasure chamber — of course it was the treasure chamber — and the standoff was pure cinema: a golden idol on its pedestal, two crews, one exit. 'Take it,' the rival expedition said, 'and die rich.'

scenes.title: The Price of Gold
scenes.text: The backup team wasn't loyal — just paid. When Sam Wilder offered them the truth about the warlord's men's promises (empty) versus a share of the legitimate expedition rights (real), they lowered their weapons. Money talks. Truth talks louder.

scenes.title: The Real Treasure
scenes.text: A kid asked Sam Wilder if it was worth it — the danger, the lost years. Sam Wilder thought of the river, the ruins, the pilot Anya's hand in the rapids. 'The thing,' Sam Wilder said, 'was never the thing.'

items.description: Signature original sports feature: Jack Hart inherits an ancient map and a one-way ticket to the Coral Triangle.
items.logline: Jack Hart inherits an ancient map and a one-way ticket to the Coral Triangle.
items.synopsis:
ACT 1 — The Call of the Wild
They made camp under strange stars. an ancient map pulsed on Jack Hart's chest. Somewhere out there, the smuggler queen was moving. The race, Jack Hart thought, was already on. sports — time to prove it.

ACT 2 — Into the Green
Jack Hart laughed, coughed river, and lived. That night they found the first marker — an ancient carving that matched an ancient map exactly. The legend was real. It had always been real.

ACT 3 — The Ruins
Jack Hart took it and ran, because Jack Hart is not an idiot. The chase through the collapsing ruins was the kind of thing they'd tell for years: swinging, sliding, the pilot Anya with the rope, an ancient map in the bag, the whole place coming down.

ACT 4 — The Price of Gold
The backup team wasn't loyal — just paid. When Jack Hart offered them the truth about the warlord's men's promises (empty) versus a share of the legitimate expedition rights (real), they lowered their weapons. Money talks. Truth talks louder.

ACT 5 — The Real Treasure
A kid asked Jack Hart if it was worth it — the danger, the lost years. Jack Hart thought of the river, the ruins, the pilot Anya's hand in the rapids. 'The thing,' Jack Hart said, 'was never the thing.'

ACT 6 — Next Horizon
Jack Hart took one last look at the Coral Triangle, green and gold and dangerous. It had given them an ancient map, and taken nothing they weren't willing to give. Fair trade.

scenes.title: Into the Green
scenes.text: The machete nearly ended it: rapids, a broken rope, Jack Hart in the water with an ancient map in a waterproof bag and the pilot Anya's hand the only solid thing in the world. 'Never leave a friend behind,' the pilot Anya gasped. 'Your rule.'

scenes.title: The Ruins
scenes.text: the mercenary Voss's team hit them in the treasure chamber — of course it was the treasure chamber — and the standoff was pure cinema: an ancient map on its pedestal, two crews, one exit. 'Take it,' the rival expedition said, 'and die rich.'

scenes.title: The Price of Gold
scenes.text: the rival expedition was delivered to the authorities with the evidence. an ancient map was delivered to the museum, on loan, with Jack Hart's name on the plaque and the pilot Anya's name right beside it, where it belonged.

scenes.title: The Real Treasure
scenes.text: the warlord's men got fifteen years and a memoir deal. Jack Hart got the kid's wide eyes and the pilot Anya's friendship and a new map already arriving by courier. No return address. Of course.

items.title: The Dark Knight
items.logline: The superhero film as crime epic — the genre's peak.
items.synopsis: Batman, Gordon, and DA Harvey Dent wage war on Gotham's mob — until the Joker, a chaos agent in smeared makeup, turns the city's soul into his battleground. The Joker's escalating atrocities (the bank heist, the assassinations, the ferries) push Dent into Two-Face and Batman to the edge of his code. In the climax, Batman takes the blame for Dent's murders to preserve the city's hope, becoming the Dark Knight — the hero Gotham deserves, but not the one it needs right now. Ledger's posthumous Oscar-winning performance redefined screen villainy.

items.title: Wonder Woman
items.logline: The superheroine's landmark — hope as power.
items.synopsis: On the hidden island of Themyscira, the Amazon princess Diana — raised on tales of Ares — leaves with the spy Steve Trevor to end World War I, believing the war is the god's work. In London and the trenches, Diana's idealism collides with human complexity: the war isn't Ares's spell, but humanity's choice. The true Ares — Sir Patrick — reveals himself; Diana defeats him not with the Godkiller sword but with the realization that love, not vengeance, is her power. Steve's sacrifice (the plane, the gas) teaches her what humanity is worth saving for.

items.title: The Station Meridian Gambit
items.description: Signature original superhero feature: Commander Ash Korv and Engineer Pip Solano take a distress beacon across Station Meridian with Pirate Queen Vex on their
items.logline: Commander Ash Korv and Engineer Pip Solano take a distress beacon across Station Meridian with Pirate Queen Vex on their trail.
items.synopsis:
ACT 1 — Launch
Commander Ash Korv gave the order anyway. The engines lit, the deck hummed, and the ship leapt toward a distress beacon with Station Meridian falling behind. Some cargoes, Commander Ash Korv knew, are worth the whole sky.

ACT 2 — The Chart Unfolds
In the quiet after, Commander Ash Korv played the starlog again. The voice — old, tired, kind — said: 'Whoever finds this, Station Meridian needs you. Hurry.' Commander Ash Korv set the course and did not look back.

ACT 3 — Storm Season
A mine took their port array. The deck went dark, then red. Engineer Pip Solano was already moving, cable in teeth, splicing by feel. 'Talk to me,' Commander Ash Korv said, and Engineer Pip Solano talked — numbers, jokes, anything to keep the fear small.

ACT 4 — The Traitor's Price
Commander Ash Korv let them live, confined to quarters. 'Pirate Queen Vex trades in hostages,' Commander Ash Korv told the crew. 'We trade in something better.' It was a gamble; the crew's eyes said they knew it.

ACT 5 — The Grid Awakens
Silence, then. The grid humming. Station Meridian safe below. Engineer Pip Solano put a hand on Commander Ash Korv's shoulder and said what everyone was thinking: 'We live.'

ACT 6 — Home Signal
Commander Ash Korv stood on the hull at sunset, watching Station Meridian turn below. superhero — the stars had taught it, and the crew had proved it, and the grid would remember it.

scenes.title: The Chart Unfolds
scenes.text: The crew voted — that was Commander Ash Korv's rule, always a vote before a suicide run. Every hand went up. Engineer Pip Solano grinned. 'We didn't sign on for safe,' they said.

scenes.title: Storm Season
scenes.text: Through the fire they saw it: Warlord Krell's flagship, waiting in the storm's eye like a spider. 'They knew the route,' Commander Ash Korv said. 'Someone sold the starlog.' The betrayal sat cold in their stomach.

scenes.title: The Traitor's Price
scenes.text: Engineer Pip Solano caught them at the airlock. There was no fight — only the traitor crying that the Hollow Fleet held their family. Commander Ash Korv understood, and hated understanding. Mercy, out here, was a luxury with teeth.

scenes.title: The Grid Awakens
scenes.text: The flagship came on anyway, and Commander Ash Korv met it ship to ship above the burning sky. It was Admiral Sarn themselves on the viewscreen, offering one last deal. Commander Ash Korv answered with the engines at full burn.
