items.title: Stars Over New Ceres Colony
items.description: Signature original superhero feature: The last ship out of New Ceres Colony carries Pilot Juna Kael, Medic Ren Okafor, and an alien engine core.
items.logline: The last ship out of New Ceres Colony carries Pilot Juna Kael, Medic Ren Okafor, and an alien engine core.
items.synopsis:
ACT 1 — Launch
They grappled an alien engine core with the cargo arm as the first raider shells crossed their bow. Medic Ren Okafor whooped as the airlock sealed. Whatever an alien engine core was, it was theirs now — and Admiral Sarn knew it.

ACT 2 — The Chart Unfolds
Medic Ren Okafor cracked an alien engine core's casing with a spanner and a prayer. Inside: coordinates, a starlog, a voice saying one word over and over — the name of New Ceres Colony.

ACT 3 — Storm Season
The battle was short and ugly. Pilot Juna Kael used the storm itself as a weapon, luring the flagship into a plasma surge that stripped its shields. They escaped in the glare, hull scorched, crew cheering raggedly.

ACT 4 — The Traitor's Price
Pilot Juna Kael laughed for the first time in days. 'All this way,' they said, 'and we were carrying the lock, not the treasure.' Medic Ren Okafor was already calculating the wake-up sequence.

ACT 5 — The Grid Awakens
Medic Ren Okafor fed an alien engine core into the ancient console. For a heartbeat nothing happened — then the sky caught fire, a lattice of light wrapping New Ceres Colony like a held breath. Warlord Krell's vanguard shattered against it like waves on rock.

ACT 6 — Home Signal
And when the next distress call came — as it always does, out in the drift — the engines were already warm. There are always more skies. There is always New Ceres Colony, somewhere, needing its heroes.

program:
"""Working demo for this playlist record: renderer + play-order simulator.
Run:  python3 playlist_demo.py          (prints the full playlist document)
      python3 playlist_demo.py play    (simulates playing it in order)
"""
import json, sys, time

PL = {'title': 'Superhero — Complete Movie Night', 'theme': 'superhero', 'week': 'L17', 'items': [{'n': 1, 'title': 'The Dark Knight', 'detail': 'Christopher Nolan'}, {'n': 2, 'title': 'Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse', 'detail': 'Bob Persichetti, Peter Ramsey, Rodney Rothman'}, {'n': 3, 'title': 'Avengers: Endgame', 'detail': 'Anthony Russo, Joe Russo'}, {'n': 4, 'title': 'Wonder Woman', 'detail': 'Patty Jenkins'}, {'n': 5, 'title': 'The Station Meridian Gambit', 'detail': 'Signature Pictures'}, {'n': 6, 'title': 'Stars Over New Ceres Colony', 'detail': 'Signature Pictures'}, {'n': 7, 'title': 'Beacon of the Valtor Nebula', 'detail': 'Signature Pictures'}, {'n': 8, 'title': 'The Void Between', 'detail': 'Signature Pictures'}], 'curator_notes': 'Superhero night 17: open with a beloved classic, follow with a Signature original, and close with the strongest film of the eight. Four public classics anchor the night; four Signature features show what comes next. Every entry is the full treatment.'}

def render():
    print("=" * 64)
    print(PL["title"].upper())
    print(PL["theme"])
    print("=" * 64)
    for it in PL["items"]:
        print("%2d. %s — %s" % (it["n"], it["title"], it["detail"]))
    print("\n--- curator notes ---\n" + PL["curator_notes"])

def play():
    render()
    print("\n▶ now playing (simulated order):")
    for it in PL["items"]:
        print("  ♪ %s ..." % it["title"])
        time.sleep(0.15)
    print("■ end of playlist — %d items" % len(PL["items"]))

if __name__ == "__main__":
    (play if len(sys.argv) > 1 and sys.argv[1] == "play" else render)()

items.title: The Silence of the Lambs
items.logline: The thriller as psychological duel — horror's Oscar.
items.synopsis: FBI trainee Clarice Starling seeks the imprisoned Hannibal Lecter's help catching the serial killer Buffalo Bill, who skins his victims. Lecter — brilliant, cannibalistic, terrifyingly polite — trades clues for Clarice's memories, in a battle of wits conducted through glass. The investigation leads to the wrong suspect (the film's famous misdirect) while Bill holds his latest victim in a pit. Clarice finds the house alone, kills Bill in the dark (his night-vision vs. her hearing), and graduates — as Lecter escapes, calling to promise he won't come for her: 'the world is more interesting with you in it.'

items.title: Se7en
items.logline: The serial-killer thriller — darkness perfected.
items.synopsis: In a rain-soaked unnamed city, the retiring detective Somerset and the hotheaded Mills hunt a killer who murders according to the seven deadly sins — each crime a grotesque tableau (gluttony, greed, sloth...). The investigation is a descent: the killer, John Doe, surrenders with two sins left, leading the detectives to a desert road. The box contains Mills's wife's head; Doe goads Mills into wrath — shooting him — completing the cycle. Somerset's closing words ('Ernest Hemingway once wrote...') offer the film's bleak moral: the world is worth fighting for, barely.

items.title: The Fugitive
items.logline: The chase thriller — perfected.
items.synopsis: Dr. Richard Kimble is wrongly convicted of his wife's murder and escapes when his prison bus crashes. U.S. Marshal Sam Gerard leads the manhunt — 'I don't care' about Kimble's innocence — while Kimble, in Chicago, hunts the one-armed man who killed his wife. The investigation reveals the pharmaceutical conspiracy (the Provasic cover-up) and the true killer. The climax — the hotel rooftop, the fight with Nichols — exonerates Kimble; Gerard, convinced at last, lowers his cuffs: the innocent man free, the marshal's respect earned.

items.title: North by Northwest
items.logline: The wrong-man thriller — Hitchcock at his most fun.
items.synopsis: Ad executive Roger Thornhill is mistaken for the spy George Kaplan and plunged into a Hitchcockian nightmare: kidnapped, framed for murder at the U.N., and chased across America by the spymaster Vandamm. Aided (and betrayed, and re-aided) by the blonde Eve Kendall, Thornhill endures the crop-duster attack, the Mount Rushmore auction, and the cliffhanger finale — literally, on the presidents' faces. The MacGuffin (microfilm) barely matters; the film is pure chase, culminating in the train's tunnel — the most famous cut in innuendo.

items.viewing_guide: Watch Hitchcock's lightness — this is the Master at play, and Grant is his perfect straight man. The final shot (the train, the tunnel) is the joke that ends the film.

items.logline: the medic Ada is taken by the Algorithm; a memory vial is Dane Kim's only leverage.
items.synopsis:
ACT 1 — Contraband
the medic Ada took one look and went pale. 'This is pre-Collapse,' the medic Ada whispered. 'the Patrol killed people for less than this. We have to move. Now.'

ACT 2 — The Network
the Algorithm noticed. Of course the Patrol noticed — the Algorithm sees all. Patrols doubled. The static got louder. Friends started disappearing from the usual corners.

ACT 3 — Blackout
'Now,' said the medic Ada. And the Undercity — all of the Undercity, every screen, every speaker — remembered.

ACT 4 — The Remembering
the Patrol responded the only way the Patrol knew: force. The Patrol marched. The drones rose. And the people of the Undercity — who had just remembered green, and laughter, and sky — stood in the streets and would not move.

ACT 5 — After the Static
There were trials. the Consortium's people faced justice — real justice, not the Algorithm's kind, with evidence and mercy both. Some were guilty. Some were just afraid. Dane Kim learned the difference matters.

ACT 6 — The Habit of Freedom
Sometimes Dane Kim walks to the tower and looks out over the Undercity, green in the cracks of the concrete, alive in the way of things that remember. a memory vial is gone. What it carried isn't.

items.logline: The war film — sacrifice examined.
items.synopsis: After D-Day, Captain Miller's squad is sent to find Private James Ryan — the last surviving brother of four — and bring him home. The mission's morality is debated through the hedgerows: the medic's death, the prisoner dilemma, the sniper's duel. They find Ryan, who refuses to leave his unit; Miller's squad defends the bridge at Ramelle against German armor. The battle costs nearly all of them; Miller's dying words — 'Earn this' — haunt the elderly Ryan at the Normandy cemetery, asking his wife if he's lived a good life.

Munny — drunk, grieving, transformed — rides into Big Whiskey and kills Little Bill and his men in the film's devastating saloon shootout. The title card reframes everything: Munny's legend, and the film's thesis on violence's cost.

items.synopsis: In the 1870s, the 14-year-old Mattie Ross hires the drunken, one-eyed Marshal Rooster Cogburn to hunt Tom Chaney, who murdered her father. The climax — Cogburn's 'Fill your hands, you son of a bitch!' charge against four riders — saves Mattie, who kills Chaney but is snakebit. The epilogue: Mattie, armless and unmarried, visits Cogburn's grave — the adventure's cost, tallied.

items.title: Shane
items.logline: The western as myth — the gunfighter's farewell.
items.synopsis: The mysterious gunfighter Shane rides into a Wyoming homesteader's valley, befriended by the Starrett family — Joe, Marian, and the boy Joey, who idolizes him. The cattle baron Ryker wants the homesteaders gone; his hired gun Wilson provokes the conflict. Shane tries to leave the gun behind (the stump-pulling, the saloon brawl he avoids), but when Ryker's men threaten Joe, Shane takes up his gun once more: the final showdown with Wilson, witnessed by Joey. Wounded, Shane rides off — 'a man has to be what he is' — as Joey cries, 'Shane! Come back!'

"""Working demo for this playlist record: renderer + play-order simulator.
Run:  python3 playlist_demo.py          (prints the full playlist document)
      python3 playlist_demo.py play    (simulates playing it in order)
"""
import json, sys, time

PL = {'title': 'Western — Complete Movie Night', 'theme': 'western', 'week': 'L20', 'items': [{'n': 1, 'title': 'The Good, the Bad and the Ugly', 'detail': 'Sergio Leone'}, {'n': 2, 'title': 'Unforgiven', 'detail': 'Clint Eastwood'}, {'n': 3, 'title': 'True Grit', 'detail': 'Joel Coen, Ethan Coen'}, {'n': 4, 'title': 'Shane', 'detail': 'George Stevens'}, {'n': 5, 'title': 'The Long Ride', 'detail': 'Signature Pictures'}, {'n': 6, 'title': 'The Long Ride', 'detail': 'Signature Pictures'}, {'n': 7, 'title': 'The Last Stage', 'detail': 'Signature Pictures'}, {'n': 8, 'title': 'The Last Stage', 'detail': 'Signature Pictures'}], 'curator_notes': 'Western night 20: open with a beloved classic, follow with a Signature original, and close with the strongest film of the eight. Four public classics anchor the night; four Signature features show what comes next. Every entry is the full treatment.'}

def render():
    print("=" * 64)
    print(PL["title"].upper())
    print(PL["theme"])
    print("=" * 64)
    for it in PL["items"]:
        print("%2d. %s — %s" % (it["n"], it["title"], it["detail"]))
    print("\n--- curator notes ---\n" + PL["curator_notes"])

def play():
    render()
    print("\n▶ now playing (simulated order):")
    for it in PL["items"]:
        print("  ♪ %s ..." % it["title"])
        time.sleep(0.15)
    print("■ end of playlist — %d items" % len(PL["items"]))

if __name__ == "__main__":
    (play if len(sys.argv) > 1 and sys.argv[1] == "play" else render)()
